tldr: The RR-MP framework uses multiple collaborative reactive and reflection agents to enhance LLM reasoning accuracy in complex scientific tasks, preventing the Degeneration-of-Thought that plagues single-agent self-reflection.
contributions: Proposes the Reactive and Reflection agents with Multi-Path Reasoning (RR-MP) framework as a post-hoc error-correction approach for complex scientific reasoning
Introduces a multi-path reasoning mechanism with parallel reactive agents generating diverse reasoning paths to improve accuracy and robustness
Conducts comparative analysis of reactive and reflection agents under various prompt types and communication modes (collaboration vs. debate)
Provides theoretical proof that increasing the number of reasoning paths reduces error probability
methods: The RR-MP framework employs a multi-path reasoning mechanism where each path consists of a reactive agent (generating preliminary answers) and a reflection agent (analyzing and refining those answers) collaborating through a shared memory module. Multiple diverse reasoning paths are generated using role-playing prompts (e.g., physicists and mathematicians), and a summarizer consolidates insights across paths. The approach requires no additional training and was tested in zero-shot and few-shot (5 examples) settings on three MMLU datasets: College Physics, College Mathematics, and Moral Scenarios, using gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 as the backbone model.
results: The Different-Domain Collaboration paradigm achieved the best overall performance with an average accuracy of 75.94%, outperforming all baselines. In few-shot settings, Different-Domain Collaboration reached 89.21% on College Physics and 91.18% on College Mathematics, significantly exceeding single-path variants (e.g., Single-Domain Collaboration: 85.29% and 86.27% respectively). Same-Domain Debate achieved 87.25% on Physics (few-shot). The method significantly outperformed baselines including Chain-of-Thought, Self-Consistency, and Self-Refine in zero-shot settings.
limitations: Resource limitations restricted experiments to gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 as the backbone model
Single-agent self-reflection remains prone to Degeneration-of-Thought, where agents become incapable of generating novel insights once confident in erroneous initial responses
The multi-path approach increases computational overhead compared to single-agent methods
The framework's effectiveness relies on the quality of role-playing prompts and agent specialization
